newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition puts off oil price decision again.
newsitem.headline: India coalition puts off oil price decision again.

text.p: India's ruling coalition, divided over how to control a mounting bill for oil subsidies, on Wednesday postponed a decision on whether to raise domestic petroleum prices, an alliance spokesman said.
The United Front's decision-making Steering Committee, ranging from free traders to communists, met for 30 minutes but for the fourth time in three months deferred the decision.
"It has not been resolved," Information Minister Jaipal Reddy, who is coalition spokesman, told reporters after the United Front committee met for 30 minutes.

"We will meet very soon to take a final view on oil prices," Reddy said. "There was a feeling today that the decision on oil prices could not be put off for too long and we should meet very soon, though no date could be fixed."
At the end of March, the government owed $4.3 billion to state oil firms, which sells some petroleum products such as kerosene to consumers at prices below world levels.
Communists in the 15-party coalition have strongly opposed proposals to raise the prices of some products, arguing that the move would hurt the poor.
